title: Linux in a Tab
subtitle: How wasm-vm streams a disk, joins a tailnet, and freezes a machine

chapters.title: Only the Blocks You Touch
chapters.blurb: A 768 MB ext4 image cut into 6,144 content-addressed 128 KiB chunks, fetched and hash-verified one guest read at a time — and the recorded boot profile showing that 100 chunks, about 1.5% of the disk, is all it takes to reach a login prompt.

chapters.title: The Tab Is the Node
chapters.blurb: Unmodified Alpine gets an ordinary lease from a network stack compiled into the emulator; packets terminate there and become framed sessions carried by a Worker that is itself the tailnet node — with window credit for backpressure and an ACL test that proves whose identity is on the wire.

chapters.title: Freeze the Machine, Restore It Anywhere
chapters.blurb: A running machine serialized into a tagged container with zero-elided RAM, locked to its build, kernel and overlay generation, streamed into IndexedDB a megabyte at a time — so a page load restores in about a second instead of executing a forty-second Linux boot.

chapters.title: Rewind: Keyframes and a Log
chapters.blurb: Why a snapshot per instruction is 100 TB/s of nonsense, why keyframes plus a log of inputs is the real design, and an honest ledger of what this machine already has for time travel — determinism gated in CI, instruction-boundary keyframes, dirty-page maps, a deduping store, one hart — against what it still needs.

chapters.title: The Swarm Is the Mirror
chapters.blurb: The same content-addressed chunks published as a torrent: the storage bucket demoted to web seed, browser tabs trading the hot 1.5% peer-to-peer, guest reads jumping the queue as critical pieces while background fill continues — and per-piece availability doubling as a crowd-sourced boot profile.
